title: Bay Area Open Science Group - OpenADMET - Raising the bar on ADMET prediction with open science
description:
This month, Dr. Pat Walters is joining us to talk about the OpenADMET initiative. Drug discovery programs frequently stall due to the Avoid-ome, which comprises the complex off-target interactions and ADMET liabilities that traditional heuristic methods struggle to address. To solve this, OpenADMET combines high-resolution structural biology, directed data generation, and machine learning into a systematic framework for predicting and mitigating these liabilities. Central to this mission is generating targeted datasets to host large-scale blind benchmarks that test community predictive models on real-world drug design problems. By uniting hundreds of academic and industry teams through these challenges, webinars, and conferences, the initiative fosters widespread collaboration to establish transparent, data-driven standards across the field.
 
The Bay Area Open Science Group is a growing community for Bay Area academics and researchers interested in incorporating open science into their research, teaching, and learning. Targeting students, faculty, and staff at UCSF, Berkeley, and Stanford, the goal of the community is to increase awareness of and engagement with all things open science, including open access articles, open research data, open source software, and open educational resources. Through this work the group hopes to connect researchers with tools they can use to make the products and process of science more equitable and reproducible.

title: Industry Documents Library Virtual Office Hour
description:
At Office Hours, you can get help searching the Industry Documents Library and learn how to use the archive. Our archivists will provide direct support during the session. Examples of topics discussed in previous IDL office hours include:

  • Tips and tricks for organizing your research on the IDL website
  • Insight into the scope of newer collections
  • Forming Boolean searches
  • Exporting citations
  • Searching by date
  • Search and view internal Slack and messaging documents
  • Newest features and improved website functionality
  • Questions about how to find certain document types

Please come ready with your questions! Join us at any time during the hour. Questions are answered on a first-come, first-served basis. We also welcome members of our user community to stay after their questions have been answered to listen as others' questions are answered live.

title: Funding Opportunities and Writing Grant Applications with AI
description:
Class Overview 

This workshop explores how to use databases and AI for finding funding opportunities and preparing grant applications. Gabe Murphy and Vincent Chan of the Office of Collaborative Research join us to present in this session of the AI in Your Toolkit 2026-2027 series.

Participants will learn about tools such as PIVOT and a new AI-driven resource developed by the Office of Collaborative Research for finding funding; discuss how to use and not use AI use when writing grant applications and reviewing other's proposals; and consider how to protect unpublished work and disclose AI use according to funder guidelines. Participants will have the opportunity for hands-on practice with PIVOT, ChatGPT Enterprise, and other resources.

Learning Objectives

  • Identify appropriate research funders using targeted funding opportunity resources

  • Assess how to use AI to assist with preparing grant applications within funder guidelines

  • Incorporate ethical principles of confidentiality and disclosure in writing and reviewing grant proposals

Presenters

Gabe Murphy, PhD, Senior Research Development Strategist, UCSF Office of Collaborative Research

Gabe ran a Neurobiology-focused laboratory for more than a decade. For the past ~5 years he has helped faculty to identify: (i) their short- and long-term research goals; (ii) funding mechanisms that are likely to support the work they’d like to do; and (iii) compelling ways to describe the insights their work will generate.

Vincent Chan, PhD, Associate Professor and Director, UCSF Office of Collaborative Research

 

Anneliese Taylor, MLIS, Head of Scholarly Communication, UCSF Library

Anneliese provides guidance to UCSF students, faculty, and staff on scholarly communication topics. She is an expert in scholarly publishing, open access models and policies, author copyrights, researcher identity platforms, and systems for capturing and assessing research attention and impact.
